title: Dependency traffic lanes: contracts and automated reassignment runbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Repeated missed handoffs during cross-team cutovers (Eng / Design / Security / Infra) are creating last-minute scope cuts and incident risk. Current dependency tracking is a flat list with ad-hoc SLAs and manual escalation. Goal: define a lane-based dependency contract model (Traffic Lanes) with explicit response and delivery SLAs, owner escalation paths, and an automated reassignment policy when teams miss commitments. This ticket covers the PM-runbook, the acceptance criteria, stakeholder alignment, and the minimal automation required to integrate with Linear + Slack + Console heatmap.
objectives: Create three lane levels (Green/Yellow/Red) with standardized SLAs and required artifact attachments
Draft contract templates for owner responsibilities and escalation points per lane
Define automated reassignment rules and a safe fallback model to maintain progress
Surface lane state in a lightweight Console dashboard and Linear view for cross-team visibility
Reduce missed handoffs and unplanned cut scope by 60% for Q2 launches
proposed_solution: Traffic lane model: Green = low-risk (7d response SLA), Yellow = medium-risk (72h response SLA + weekly sync), Red = blockers (24h response + on-call escalation)
Owner ledger: per-dependency fields for owner, backup owner, lane, SLA timestamps, last-contact log
Automation: scheduled checks (cron) that compare timestamps and trigger reassignment notification to backup owner if primary owner exceeds SLA + configured grace period
Integrations: create Linear custom fields + status board, Slack channel pings for overdue, Console heatmap tile showing lane density by project
Safety: reassignment creates a 'handoff checklist' artifact and a temporary read-only flag on implementation work until new owner acknowledges
acceptance_criteria: Lane definitions and contract templates published in Confluence and signed off by Eng, Design, Security, Infra
Linear board with lane custom field created and synced to Console; at least 2 pilot projects using it
Automation triggers reassignment in staging for simulated overdue events (unit test coverage >= 70%)
Console heatmap shows lane counts and the 7/30/90 day trend; PMs can filter by team and project
Reduction target plan documented (baseline metrics captured) and measurement dashboard wired
rollout_plan: Week 1: Stakeholder workshop and contract iteration (Eng leads, Design PMs, Security, Infra ops)
Week 2: Linear custom fields + board + Confluence templates; Design creates Figma microflow for handoff checklist
Week 3: Build automation lambda (checks + reassignment) and wire Slack/Linear notifications; run closed beta with 2 initiatives
Week 4: Collect pilot feedback, iterate contracts, expand to 6 teams; toggle automation to production
Post-launch (Q2): Measure impact, tune SLAs, add PagerDuty integration for Red lane if needed
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Automated reassignment may interrupt ongoing work — Mitigation: add grace period and require new owner acknowledgement before changing implementation state
Risk: Teams ignore lane labels — Mitigation: require lane field during dependency creation for initiatives in release window
Risk: Permission boundaries prevent reassignment — Mitigation: Engineering to add scoped service account and audit log; Security review required
Risk: Signal noise from low-signal dependencies — Mitigation: provide guidance and a quick triage checklist to classify dependency severity
